transcript:
Live from NPR News in Washington on Corva Coleman, a commercial flight traveling from
Dubai in the United Arab Emirates to Tel Aviv, Israel was forced to make an emergency landing
today.
That was after it issued an emergency alert on board.
Both the pilot and co-pilot have been hospitalized.
NPR's Kat Lamsdorf reports from Tel Aviv exactly what happened aboard is unclear.
The flight of a plane made an emergency landing at Tabuk Airport near the Jordanian border
in Saudi Arabia.
In a statement, a spokesperson for Fly Dubai acknowledged that the flight "experienced
an incident" while en route from Dubai to Tel Aviv, and said that all passengers are
safe and accounted for, but did not offer more details.
Saudi authorities said they received a distress call from the flight, and that the flight's
pilot and co-pilot were hospitalized upon landing after sustaining injuries on board.
No further information was provided on the nature of those injuries or how they came
about.
Israeli Prime Minister Benjamin Netanyahu is holding consultations over the incident
and "monitoring developments," his office said.
Kat Lamsdorf, NPR News, Tel Aviv.
The Pentagon says the U.S. military has officially withdrawn from Iraq, and PR's Jan Araf is
in Baghdad.
This isn't the first time the U.S. has withdrawn in 2011 after a disagreement with Iraq over
the status of U.S. forces here.
They left, and then they were invited back by Iraq three years later to fight ISIS.
So they've stayed since then as part of the U.S.-led international coalition that has
been fighting the militant group.
So Iraqi leaders and U.S. commanders held a ceremony in Baghdad, closed to the press,
but to be carried live by state TV, which is also showing drone footage of sprawling
U.S. bases that are now empty.
NPR's Jan Araf reporting.
NPR has learned of a plan for a massive new data center on federal land in Utah.
NPR's Jeff Brumfield reports it would involve building hundreds of nuclear reactors.
The proposal seen by NPR came from the company Valor Atomics.
Valor already has a test reactor operating in Utah, but it wants to build around 450
more small nuclear reactors on 9,000 acres of federal land.
The reactors would provide power for data centers, among other things.
Neil Clark with the Southern Utah Wilderness Alliance says Valor isn't the only company
quietly seeking to build data centers on public lands.
It's pretty obvious that they're trying to keep these proposals and these processes
totally under the radar to make sure the public is kept in the dark.
The Bureau of Land Management says the public will have an opportunity to comment on the
proposal after the agency reviews the application for completeness.
Jeff Brumfield, NPR News.
A government report on inflation that's watched by the Federal Reserve says inflation rose
a little less than expected last month.
This report says inflation is running at an annual rate of 3.4 percent.
This is NPR.
The Pentagon says Defense Secretary Pete Hegseth is going to announce more cuts to the number
of generals and admirals serving in the U.S. military.
He has already ordered a 10 percent cut to the flag and general officer positions.
Hegseth will now double that to a 20 percent cut by the end of the year.
The Mammoth Farm Bill is set to expire at the end of the day today.
Congress is deadlocked over the legislation typically passed every five years.
The program supports agriculture, and the current economy is already dire for many of
the nation's farmers.
The Education Department is extending the enrollment period for student loan borrowers
to lower their interest rates, and Pierre Sequoia Carrillo explains.
Nearly 2 million federal student loan borrowers have already enrolled in auto pay and reduced
their interest rate for the next two years.
The initiative, announced by the Department of Education this summer, aims to get more
borrowers back to regular repayment after the COVID-19 payment freeze.
The Department said borrower participation in auto pay dropped from 83 percent in 2019
to just 40 percent in 2025.
Borrowers now have until the end of the calendar year, December 31, to enroll in auto pay.
Those already enrolled in the program do not need to take any action to receive the benefit.
Sequoia Carrillo, NPR News.
There's a winner in the Fat Bear Week contest.
It's the brown bear backpack.
He's estimated to weigh more than a thousand pounds.
The contest is held every year by Katmai National Park and Preserve in Alaska.
This is NPR.

topics.text: Commercial flight from Dubai to Tel Aviv makes emergency landing in Saudi Arabia after incident
Pentagon announces U.S. military has officially withdrawn from Iraq after two-decade presence
Company Valor Atomics proposes building 450 small nuclear reactors on federal land in Utah
Government inflation report shows annual inflation rate running at 3.4 percent
Defense Secretary Pete Hegseth doubles planned cuts to military generals and admirals to 20 percent
Farm Bill set to expire at end of day as Congress remains deadlocked
Education Department extends enrollment deadline for student loan borrowers to reduce interest rates
Brown bear known as Backpack wins Fat Bear Week contest in Alaska
